solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cup of tea left to get very cold

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea
ice is the very cold stuff, the extreme of chill

explanation.surface: A cup of tea is abandoned and goes stone cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet used at communion or as a ceremonial drinking vessel is a kind of cup.

clue.text: One gives hand in bringing them together

definitions.text: One gives hand in bringing them together

parts.words: One gives hand in bringing them together
parts.note: one who gives someone a hand, applause, by bringing the palms together

explanation.surface: Someone lends a hand by uniting a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives hand' suggests helping or a marriage, but here it is a round of applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone applauding strikes the palms together, so gives a hand in that sense.

clue.text: An Italian city and southern capital

parts.note: Napoli is the Italian name for Naples

explanation.surface: A city in Italy alongside a capital in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maryland city, home of the US Naval Academy, is the state's capital.

clue.text: Lazybones strangely riled

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters of riled are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lazy person is oddly angry.
explanation.definitionFit: A layabout who does no work is a synonym for a lazybones.

clue.text: A1 spy nobbled entering facility? No problem!

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the jumbled letters sit within the ease word

parts.note: facility means ease, as in doing something with facility

indicators.note: nobbled means tampered with, so the letters of A1 spy are disordered

parts.note: A1 is written AI, the 1 standing in for the letter I

explanation.surface: A top spy is got at while infiltrating a facility, effortlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facility' looks like a building but means ease of doing; 'nobbled' scrambles the letters and 'entering' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describing a very simple task is an exclamation that something is no trouble at all.

clue.text: Female commander, no longer fresh, concentrated

parts.note: OC stands for officer commanding
something used is second-hand, no longer new

explanation.surface: A female officer, tired out, is still concentrating hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Attention that is concentrated is directed on one point, a synonym.

clue.text: Fine hair and waste wool

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
a lock is a tress of hair

explanation.surface: Fine hair and scraps of wool, as on a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Tufts of waste wool or cotton used for stuffing are called by this name.

clue.text: Knight caught her alive after struggle

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: after a struggle the letters of her alive end up rearranged

explanation.surface: A knight captures a woman alive following a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A French title for a member of an order of knighthood, so a knight.

clue.text: Four characters from the Bard old hat

indicators.note: only the opening four letters of the playwright's name are kept

parts.note: the Bard is Shakespeare

explanation.surface: Four roles from Shakespeare are worn out, old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hat' reads as one phrase meaning stale, but 'old' gives O and 'hat' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall cylindrical military cap with a peak is a type of hat.

clue.text: Everyone on island to stop the German one loitering

indicators.note: to stop means to plug, so the letters fill the middle of the German article

parts.note: der is a German word for the
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Islanders unite to halt a German who hangs about.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dawdles or lingers is loitering, a near synonym.

clue.text: Invalidate yearbook where second article expunged

indicators.note: expunged means struck out, so the article is removed from the yearbook

parts.note: an annual is a book published once a year
A is an indefinite article, the second article after 'the'

explanation.surface: An editor voids a yearbook in which a piece has been deleted.
explanation.walkthrough: The A removed is the one in the middle of the yearbook word, not the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To cancel a marriage or law, declaring it void, is to invalidate it.

clue.text: Obstruct and delay, admitting nothing topical

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the delay word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: to stall is to delay
O looks like zero, nothing
something topical is new, current news

explanation.surface: Someone stalls a discussion, refusing to talk about current affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obstruct and delay' looks like one definition, but 'delay' is wordplay. 'admitting' puts ONEW inside STALL.
explanation.definitionFit: To block or hold up proceedings with evasive tactics is to obstruct them.

clue.text: Essay introducing second book

indicators.note: introducing means coming before, so the essay word leads

parts.note: a paper is an essay or academic article
to second a motion is to back it, support it

explanation.surface: An essay introduces a second volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' looks like an ordinal but is the verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: A softcover edition is a type of book.

clue.text: Excellent oil shaken to make mayonnaise

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, excellent, written here as AI

indicators.note: shaken means mixed up, so the letters of oil are rearranged

explanation.surface: Good oil is shaken to emulsify into mayonnaise.
explanation.definitionFit: This garlic sauce from Provence is a type of mayonnaise.

clue.text: Trace local banished from country for example

indicators.note: banished from means thrown out of, so the pub is removed from the country word

parts.note: a republic is an example of a country
in Britain one's local is one's nearby pub

explanation.surface: A trace of the local is expelled from the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' as a noun is British slang for a neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A surviving remnant or vestige of the past is a trace of it.

clue.text: X-ray extending from one side to the other

definitions.text: extending from one side to the other

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross
a ray of light is a beam

explanation.surface: An X-ray image spanning the whole body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'X-ray' reads as a medical scan but splits into X, a cross, and ray, a beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal timber spanning a structure from wall to wall; the definition is descriptive.

clue.text: Bookmaker liable to be damned?

parts.note: plays on the Duke of Wellington's retort 'publish and be damned': a firm that makes books might well be damned for what it prints

explanation.surface: A betting shop owner risks damnation for his trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookmaker' suggests a bookie taking bets, but here it means a firm that produces books.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm that issues books is literally a maker of books; the famous quotation adds the damnation.

clue.text: Wager Irish Republic will shelter no undesirable

parts.note: a bet is a wager

indicators.note: shelter means hold protectively inside, so the republic encloses no

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland

explanation.surface: A gamble that Ireland will refuse to harbour an unwanted person.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet hate, the thing or person one most dislikes, is an undesirable.

clue.text: US writer writhing around on her what?

indicators.note: writhing around means twisting about, so the letters of the words that follow are churned

explanation.surface: An American author squirming on top of a woman, puzzled.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathaniel of that surname wrote The Scarlet Letter, a famous American author.

clue.text: Gorgeous creature brought to love retreat is cheating

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
love is zero in tennis, O
a nest is a cosy retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: A beauty taken to a love nest is being unfaithful.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheating behaviour is deceitful and untruthful, a synonym.

clue.text: Stepped over unusual tailless sea creature

indicators.note: over means turned back, so the stepping word reads backwards

parts.note: paced means stepped

indicators.note: tailless means losing its final letter

parts.note: odd means unusual

explanation.surface: Someone stepped over a strange sea creature with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns PACED into DECAP, and 'tailless' trims ODD to OD.
explanation.definitionFit: A crab or lobster, with ten legs, is a marine crustacean of this order.

clue.text: Maybe king due favour had words

parts.note: R stands for rex, king, as on coins and in chess notation
someone due a favour is owed one

explanation.surface: A king who was owed a favour argued about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have words with someone is to quarrel, an idiom for a British argument.

clue.text: Disorder casts monarch into endless peril

indicators.note: casts means throws, here throwing the monarch somewhere
into means placed inside the shortened peril word
endless means without its last letter

parts.note: danger means peril
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Chaos plunges a monarch into perpetual danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the final letter of the peril word, and 'casts ... into' signals the container; ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw into confusion, to put out of order.

clue.text: Insensitive Conservative — right fool!

parts.note: C abbreviates Conservative, the British political party
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: An insensitive Tory politician is called a proper idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' reads as 'utter' in the surface but gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude, tactless behaviour shows a lack of sensitivity, a synonym.

clue.text: Stock set with food as image shows

parts.note: a pic is an informal word for a picture, an image

explanation.surface: Stock jelly with food in it, as a picture shows.
explanation.definitionFit: This savoury jelly is made from meat stock and set around pieces of food.

clue.text: Horrendous heat burns person often seen on beach

indicators.note: horrendous means dreadful, so the letters of the words that follow are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Terrible heat leaves a beachgoer burnt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lying out to soak up rays is a familiar sight at the seaside.

clue.text: Pressure in ground brings ruin

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the pressure letter goes within the ground word

parts.note: soil is the ground

explanation.surface: Pressure in the ground causes ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin something is to mar or damage it, a synonym.

clue.text: Expect a delay

parts.note: a wait is a delay

explanation.surface: Expect a hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To look out for something coming is to anticipate or expect it.

clue.text: Sprinkle liberally on one pizza topping

parts.note: to pepper something is to scatter over it thickly
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An instruction to scatter something generously over a pizza.
explanation.definitionFit: This spicy Italian-American sausage is a common pizza topping.

clue.text: Item with Oedipal strings attached?

parts.note: a man tied to his mother's ... strings is excessively attached to her, as Oedipus was

explanation.surface: A garment hinting at an unhealthy bond with mother.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'tied to his mother's apron strings' describes a man dominated by his mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The kitchen garment has ties, the strings of the idiom about mother-dependence.

clue.text: Figure boy keeping vermin should be turned over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the whole construction is read backwards
keeping means holding, so the boy word contains the vermin

parts.note: a lad is a boy
mice are household vermin

explanation.surface: A lad who keeps rodents ought to be reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' signals the container and 'should be turned over' reverses the whole result, not just the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A number written with a point and fractional digits is a kind of figure.

clue.text: Longer than usual extension supplied by engineers

indicators.note: supplied by means followed by, so the engineers come after the extension

parts.note: EXT is the abbreviation for a telephone extension
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: An unusually long extension built by engineering contractors.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the British Army's engineering corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at the far limit, well beyond the norm, exceeds the usual length or degree.
